kings.name: Adad-nirari II
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Founder of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, who reconquered lost territory and fixed Babylon's northern border.

kings.name: Ashurnasirpal II
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Warrior king who moved the capital to Kalhu (Nimrud) and campaigned to the Mediterranean.

kings.name: Shalmaneser III
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Son of Ashurnasirpal II; fought Urartu and the western coalition at Qarqar.

kings.name: Shamshi-Adad V
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Son of Shalmaneser III who put down a rebellion by his brother and campaigned against Babylon.

kings.name: Adad-nirari III
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: King of Assyria who subdued Damascus and took tribute from Syria-Palestine.

kings.name: Shalmaneser V
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Son of Tiglath-Pileser III whose siege of Samaria ended with the city's fall.

kings.name: Sargon II
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Usurper and conqueror who built Dur-Sharrukin and defeated Merodach-Baladan, Urartu and Carchemish.

kings.name: Merodach-Baladan II
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Chaldean king of Babylon who defied Assyria and was twice expelled by Sargon II.

kings.name: Esarhaddon
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Son of Sennacherib who rebuilt Babylon and conquered Egypt.

kings.name: Teumman
kings.title: King of Elam
kings.description: Elamite king defeated and killed by Ashurbanipal at the Battle of Ulai.

kings.name: Shamash-shum-ukin
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Brother of Ashurbanipal who ruled Babylon and revolted, leading to his own destruction.

kings.name: Sin-shar-ishkun
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Last king of Assyria to rule from Nineveh; died in its fall.

kings.name: Nabopolassar
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Founder of the Neo-Babylonian Empire who destroyed Assyria in alliance with the Medes.

events.name: Adad-nirari II Restores Assyrian Power
events.description: Adad-nirari II campaigns against the Aramaeans and fixes the border with Babylonia, beginning Assyria's recovery.

events.name: Ashurnasirpal II Campaigns to the Mediterranean
events.description: Ashurnasirpal II marches through Syria to the Mediterranean, exacting tribute along the Phoenician coast.

events.name: The Battle of Qarqar
events.description: Shalmaneser III fights a coalition of twelve kings including Hadadezer of Damascus and Ahab of Israel at Qarqar on the Orontes.

events.name: Shalmaneser III Campaigns Against Urartu
events.description: Shalmaneser III attacks the nascent kingdom of Urartu, sacking its capital Arzashkun.

events.name: Shamshi-Adad V Suppresses the Rebellion
events.description: Shamshi-Adad V crushes the revolt of his brother Ashur-da'in-aplu and the rebel cities.

events.name: Adad-nirari III Subdues Damascus
events.description: Adad-nirari III marches west and receives tribute from Damascus and the Levantine states.

events.name: The Eclipse of Bur-Sagale
events.description: The solar eclipse recorded in the Assyrian eponym chronicle for the year of Bur-Sagale, a key anchor of Near Eastern chronology.

events.name: Tiglath-Pileser III Conquers Arpad
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser III annexes the Syrian state of Arpad after a long siege, extending Assyrian rule over northern Syria.

events.name: Tiglath-Pileser III Defeats Urartu
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser III campaigns into Urartu, defeating Sarduri II and besieging the capital Tushpa.

events.name: The Fall of Damascus
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser III sacks Damascus and executes its king, ending Aramaean resistance in the Levant.

events.name: Tiglath-Pileser III Crowns Himself King of Babylon
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon and celebrates the New Year festival under the throne name Pulu, uniting the two crowns.

events.name: Shalmaneser V Besieges Samaria
events.description: Shalmaneser V lays siege to Samaria after the Israelite king Hoshea withholds tribute.

events.name: The Fall of Samaria
events.description: Samaria falls to Assyria (under Shalmaneser V or Sargon II) and its people are deported.

events.name: Merodach-Baladan II Seizes Babylon
events.description: The Chaldean chief Merodach-Baladan seizes Babylon and resists Assyrian attempts to dislodge him.

events.name: Sargon II Conquers Carchemish
events.description: Sargon II annexes Carchemish, the last great Hittite successor state, extending Assyria to the Euphrates bend.

events.name: Sargon II Sacks Musasir
events.description: In a lightning campaign against Urartu, Sargon II sacks the temple-city Musasir and carries off its god Haldi.

events.name: Sargon II Retakes Babylon
events.description: Sargon II drives Merodach-Baladan from Babylon and enters the city as its king.

events.name: The Death of Sargon II in Tabal
events.description: Sargon II is killed on campaign in Tabal, an unprecedented fate for an Assyrian king, and his body is never recovered.

events.name: Sennacherib's Siege of Jerusalem
events.description: Sennacherib campaigns against Judah and besieges Jerusalem; Hezekiah pays heavy tribute.

events.name: The Battle of Halule
events.description: Sennacherib fights the Babylonian-Elamite coalition at Halule on the Tigris; both sides claim victory.

events.name: Sennacherib Destroys Babylon
events.description: After repeated Babylonian revolts, Sennacherib sacks Babylon and diverts water over its ruins.

events.name: Esarhaddon Conquers Egypt
events.description: Esarhaddon invades Egypt, defeats Pharaoh Taharqa and takes Memphis, adding Egypt to the Assyrian Empire.

events.name: Esarhaddon Rebuilds Babylon
events.description: Esarhaddon begins the long rebuilding of Babylon, restoring the temples his father had destroyed.

events.name: Ashurbanipal Sacks Thebes
events.description: Ashurbanipal's army sacks the Egyptian city of Thebes, the greatest sack the ancient world had yet seen.

events.name: The Battle of Ulai
events.description: Ashurbanipal defeats and kills the Elamite king Teumman at the Battle of Ulai, celebrated in the great relief cycle.

events.name: The Revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin
events.description: Ashurbanipal's brother Shamash-shum-ukin, king of Babylon, revolts with Elamite and Arab support; Babylon falls after a long siege in 648.

events.name: Ashurbanipal Sacks Susa
events.description: Ashurbanipal destroys Susa and ravages Elam, erasing it as a rival power.

events.name: The Fall of Ashur
events.description: The Medes under Cyaxares capture and sack the Assyrian religious capital Ashur, in alliance with Nabopolassar of Babylon.

events.name: The Fall of Nineveh
events.description: The combined Medo-Babylonian army sacks Nineveh; Sin-shar-ishkun dies in the flames and the Assyrian Empire collapses.

events.name: Ashurnasirpal II Rebuilds Kalhu
events.description: Ashurnasirpal II rebuilds Kalhu (Nimrud) as his new capital, adorning it with palaces and the Northwest Palace reliefs.

events.name: Shalmaneser III Receives the Tribute of Jehu
events.description: Shalmaneser III receives tribute from Israel's king Jehu, commemorated on the Black Obelisk.

events.name: The Battle of Der
events.description: An Elamite army under Humban-nikash I defeats Sargon II at Der, checking Assyrian designs on Babylon.

events.name: Sargon II Founds Dur-Sharrukin
events.description: Sargon II founds a new capital at Dur-Sharrukin ('Fortress of Sargon'), today's Khorsabad.

events.name: Sennacherib Rebuilds Nineveh
events.description: Sennacherib transforms Nineveh into his capital, building the 'Palace Without Rival' and new waterworks.

events.name: Esarhaddon Imposes Vassal Treaties
events.description: Esarhaddon imposes loyalty treaties on vassals and courtiers to secure the succession of Ashurbanipal.

events.name: Ashurbanipal Establishes the Library of Nineveh
events.description: Ashurbanipal assembles the great cuneiform library at Nineveh, collecting tablets from across Mesopotamia.
